A B S T R A C T
In this investigation, a Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C lightweight austenitic steel has been developed through strategic
alloying with Ni and Cr elements coupled with the employment of a thermo-mechanical processing technique
featuring ultra-fast cooling. This composition and treatment synergistically transcend the conventional trade-off
between strength and ductility, positioning the mechanical performance of this steel notably above that of
comparable low-density austenitic steels previously reported. The coordinated incorporation of Ni and Cr is key
to modulating the precipitation threshold for nanoscale k-carbides and LRO domains, achieving an optimal size
for precipitate-induced strengthening. The incorporation of Cr specifically contributes to a dual enhancement
mechanism: it fosters the generation of high-density dislocation arrays (HDDA) and refines the dynamic slip band
(DSBR) during deformation, which in turn, elevates the strain hardenability and ductility. The remarkable
synergy in strength and ductility is attributed to a combination of mechanisms including grain boundary rein-
forcement, solid solution hardening, the precipitation strengthening effect of nanoscale precipitates, and the
activation of secondary slip system dislocations. This synergy is quantitatively reflected in the material's vield
strength (YS) exceeding 1100 MPa, ultimate tensile strength (UTS) surpassing 1200 MPa, and a total elongation
(TEL) exceeding 45%. The insights gained from this research provide critical guidance for the design and creation
of austenitic low-density steels that do not compromise between strength and ductility, thereby offering superior
overall performance

growth mechanism, and the different degrees of the ordered phases and
the ordered domains of LRO and κ-carbides lead to different yield
strengths [20,53]. Previous studies have shown that the addition of Al
can promote the formation of ordered phases [19,20,53]. In this study,
the steel under investigation contains not only the elements Fe, Mn, Al,

5. Conclusion
Focusing on austenitic low-density steels with compositions of
Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr (where x = 0, 2 wt% and y = 0, 3, 5 wt%),
this study leverages first-principle computational analysis, precipitation
kinetics, deformation, and fracture mechanism investigations to suc-
cessfully design a material that harmonizes exceptional strength and
ductility with superior overall performance. Furthermore, it elucidates
the intrinsic connection between microstructural features and macro-
scopic deformation behavior, with the following specific conclusions:
(1) The Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr steels exhibit superior YS, UTS,
and TEL compared to other steels in the Fe–Mn–Al–C series that
benefit from effective Ni and Cr alloying. This alloying strategy
mitigates the traditional compromise between YS, UTS, and TEL,
as demonstrated by 2Ni3Cr steels with YS exceeding 1100 MPa,
UTS surpassing 1200 MPa, and TEL greater than 45%.
(2) The strategic addition of Ni and Cr plays a pivotal role in con-
trolling the precipitation dynamics of nano-sized κ-carbides and
LRO domains, optimizing their dimensions for enhanced
precipitate-induced strengthening. Ni element adding reduces
nucleation energy barriers and facilitates the growth and stabi-
lization of κ-carbides, enhancing their efficacy in strengthening.
On the contrary, Cr elevates the nucleation energy barrier.
(3) These improvements are attributed to a synergy of grain bound-
ary strengthening, solid solution strengthening, and precipitation
strengthening. Additionally, the progressive evolution of the
microstructure under strain leads to the repeated formation and
multiplication of HDDA and DSBR duel mechanisms.
(4) The enhancement of both strength and strain hardening proper-
ties through Ni and Cr alloying is a key contribution of this study.
This approach not only elucidates the mechanisms behind the
improved properties but also sets a foundational strategy for
designing next-generation austenitic lightweight steels with su-
perior mechanical performance.
